subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps

Hi Olivia (and Raj),

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the level-setting and the demo of your current search/assist flows. Quick recap from our side to make sure we’re aligned on pain, goals, and the tests we discussed. If anything below needs correction, flag it and I’ll update.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- High latency and inconsistent tail latency on your current vendor for multi-turn support (esp. >1k tokens).
- Rising per-token costs for embedding + reranking workflows on peak traffic.
- Lack of fine-grained observability across routes makes root-cause of regressions hard to diagnose.

Goals (success criteria):
1) Match or beat current vendor on median latency (<120ms for 256-token responses) and improve 95th percentile.
2) Reduce per-response cost by ~20% using batching + cache without hurting quality.
3) Transparent tracing + per-route cost/latency dashboards for SRE and product.
4) Run a 2-week side-by-side bake-off with repeatable tests and shared evals.

Decision criteria you indicated:
- Latency (median + 95th)
- Cost per request at expected QPS
- Output quality on your in-house eval set (which Raj will share)
- Ops overhead for deployment & rollback

Open questions / items we promised to deliver:
- We’ll send a proposed test plan and a results matrix template (attached).
- Confirm availability of a trial cluster (we requested: 4x A10/80GB equiv) — Marcus to confirm provisioning timeline.
- Need Raj’s eval set and the list of critical prompts + acceptance thresholds.
- We’ll provide a sample tracing dashboard and a short runbook for failover.

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Marissa: Send bake-off matrix + test plan (attached) — today.
2) Raj: Share eval corpus + thresholds — by Tue 4/13.
3) Marcus / Dylan: Provision trial cluster and give access — target Mon 4/12.
4) Joint kickoff call to align on data ingestion and traffic routing — propose Tue 4/13 10am PT.

Attachments:
- omnihealth-bakeoff-matrix-20270410.xlsx (matrix to capture lat/cost/qual results)
- omnihealth-test-plan-20270410.pdf (detailed tests we propose)

If that all looks right, I’ll send a calendar invite for the kickoff and get the provisioning started.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

--

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@omnihealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@omnihealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Couple quick notes:

Thanks for pulling the matrix and test plan together — I reviewed the PDF and it aligns with what we discussed. A few additions:
- Please include a synthetic load test that simulates our peak 1.2k RPS spikes (we’ll provide traffic shape).
- For quality, we’ll run both automated evals and a human review on a 200-sample slice.

On provisioning: we can host a short trial in our AWS account if that’s simplest; we’ll create an IAM role for access. If Redwood can also spin up a dedicated instance in your environment for comparison, that would be helpful.

Decision timeline: our procurement team needs vendor comparison + rough TCO by 4/23. We’re planning a steering committee meeting 4/26.

Questions:
1) Can you commit to providing a 30-day log retention snapshot for the test window? We need auditables for compliance.
2) Are there any known model variants you’d recommend for lower token-cost (quantized options)?

I’ll ask Raj to share the eval set by Monday.

Best,
Olivia
Sr. Product Manager, Search & Assist | OmniHealth
olivia.chen@omnihealth.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@omnihealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps

Hi Olivia — Marcus here from the runtime team. Quick answers to your questions and a proposed ops plan.

1) Retention: We can provide a 30-day snapshot for the test window. We’ll produce a read-only audit bundle (logs, traces, alert history) at the end of the test — that’s part of the bake-off deliverable.
2) Model variants: for cost-forward tests we recommend: rwi-large-quant (8-bit) and rwi-medium-q (mixed precision). We’ll run quality checks vs the full-precision models and flag regressions in the matrix.

Ops plan (provisioning):
- Dylan: will prepare IaC to provision the trial cluster in OmniHealth’s account (we’ll need an infra role).
- Timeline: aim to have infra ready and access granted by Mon 4/12 EOD.
- Kickoff: Tue 4/13 10am PT (Marissa, Olivia, Raj, Marcus, Dylan) — we’ll walk through ingestion, eval wiring, and the first smoke tests.

One ask: Olivia/ Raj — please share the traffic shape + any IP allowlist for the trial nodes so we can preconfigure.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

- Kickoff calendar invite sent for Tue 4/13 10am PT (please accept).
- Marcus / Dylan: proceed with provisioning in OmniHealth account; Marissa to share access details once Raj provides role.

Related links: HubSpot record + MAP for signature are here — please review before the kickoff: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/9876543 and DocuSign MAP link (tracking in metadata).

Thanks — looking forward to it.
Marissa
